package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package is described in the report. The article discusses general risks and mitigation strategies for software supply chain security in CI/CD pipelines, referencing notable attacks (SolarWinds, Codecov, Kaseya) as examples of what could be prevented by following NIST SP 800-204D guidelines.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthorized code commits to CI/CD pipelines
Tampering with build artifacts or pipeline processes
Introduction of secrets or credentials into code repositories
Unverified third-party component usage in builds
Lack of artifact integrity verification before deployment
file_indicators: Presence of secrets (API keys, tokens, certificates) in source code or configuration files
Unusual or unauthorized changes to build scripts (e.g., Jenkinsfile, .github/workflows/*.yml, Dockerfiles)
Artifacts lacking cryptographic signatures or provenance metadata
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound connections from build agents to external domains
Connections to known malicious or untrusted package repositories
Unusual API calls to version control or artifact management systems
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor CI/CD pipelines for unauthorized code commits, changes to build scripts, and the presence of secrets in code. Enforce artifact integrity checks using cryptographic signatures and SBOMs. Audit network activity from build agents for unexpected external communications. Use access controls and logging to detect and alert on unauthorized or anomalous actions within the pipeline.
